beats.headline: Three candidates, and the crawler picks the lawyer
beats.text: Odette puts three of us in front of the crawlers on her show, having first announced that she will be performing as a deity of her own this season, Nekhebit, which is her affair. What the crawlers are choosing is an adjutant for the ninth floor. Carl asks me whether he has killed any of my family. I tell him: my half-sister, and nobody but my brother-in-law and nephews holds him responsible; several distant relations, which was within his rights. I recently sentenced my own aunt to indentureship for her taxes. Carl picks me.

beats.headline: First word in the Warlord Chat
beats.text: Warlords. One of you should proceed immediately to the flag room, beside the throne room in your stronghold outside the city, to oversee the final preparations and deal with the recruits arriving there. The other should remain in Larracos and enlist your fellow crawlers. The rule behind the advice: once the ceasefire ends, any crawler not already recruited may be compelled into another army as a conscript. Time is short.

beats.headline: Herman the Fleet does not get to finish
beats.text: Carl, Donut, Tipid and Florin come into the Fortress of Unyielding Power and Authority, and Florin walks them through the ceasefire rules. Then our own Elite, Herman the Fleet, leaned on by Sensation Entertainment, reveals what he actually is, which is a delivery system for a bomb. I deal with him. An adjutant may do that. It is in the rules, and I have read the rules.

beats.headline: What she says of her sister
beats.text: The Princess asks whether my sister was nice or a jerk. She means the orc queen, who died when my nephew attempted to assassinate them. Ugloo and I once had a very similar outlook on life. When she married into the royal family, she lost a great deal of who she was. We had not spoken in a long while, but before she died she wrote to ask if I would be an adjutant this season. She was going to the Scolopendra Club to meet the king. I ask why the Princess wishes to know.

beats.headline: The Gurgles, allowed
beats.text: A crawler with a flamethrower says the Gurgles is a magical attack and this is bullshit. It is an exploit. They infected the pets before the magic ban, and it has been allowed in the past. The mages ought to do a better job of keeping infections out. The Princess asks what the Gurgles are: a nasty, contagious, incurable debuff, which the factions agreed many years ago never to use again. It caused the insanity and the rabies. The truck stop pill I am not familiar with. I suspect it made them so big.

beats.headline: Too smart for your own good
beats.text: I appear beside Carl in the Prism's headquarters and tell him he is too smart for his own good. They slaughtered them back there. Does he know how many jumped blindly into that middle trench? The scout for Team Retribution went up almost twenty levels. What counts as offensive magic will need revisiting; that chemical alteration spell is a little too powerful. He ignores me, puts on his ring, and calls for the Empress.

beats.headline: The rules of the parlay
beats.text: I walk Carl and Donut up to the parlay and give them the rules before we arrive, because a parlay is a contract with a shorter fuse than most. King Rust brings Deng Bao, a Grixist, as his adjutant. Donut notices before I do that King Rust is crying.

beats.headline: A ruling about the goat
beats.text: Most of the Naga army is already dead and Prepotente did it, for what the Blood Hunter show did to Miriam Dom. Carl would like to work with him. My advice is a ruling rather than an opinion: he may not, not directly, not while Prepotente stands outside the Princess Posse. Bring the goat inside the team, or keep your distance from him.

beats.headline: Temple rules apply
beats.text: The Sultanate's adjutant arrives with a louder crack than usual: Admiral Corinne Whimpleshin, a camel in a sundress, holding a martini, calling foul. The gods. The summoning of the gods. I ask what the foul is. She wishes to stop everything. It does not matter. We have no standing. Temple rules apply, and she knows it; her team summoned the god. She says it was not the Blood Sultanate, that Carl did it and knew this would happen. Carl says he has not summoned anything. The timer ends.

beats.headline: Not a thing, until just now
beats.text: Carl, we have just been notified of a new non-team entity called the War Mage Rebellion. 'Non-team entity' is not a thing. It was not, at least, until just now. As far as I can tell, they broke their allegiance against the Skull Empire, which Conscription should not permit, with a clever combination of Pull spells, and then teleported straight to Juice Box and Ferdinand. Drick has called a foul against his own team, alleging illegal interference. It is shaky unless he can prove prior contact. A full quorum has been called. I am going to the hearing.

beats.headline: Stalling on purpose
beats.text: Carl wants to know why the adjudication is not finished and Juice Box is missing the war. Carl, trust me on this. You want this trial to go on as long as possible. We are stalling on purpose, and we will stall until the AI becomes so irritated that it calls a halt itself.

beats.headline: Two warlords for one rebellion
beats.text: The War Mage Rebellion holds the castle at Larracos, and six hours on the clock decides the floor. I run alongside Carl and give him what I have, which is less than he wants. Agatha has been named co-warlord beside Akuma, much as Ferdinand was added beside Juice Box, and nobody on that team anticipated it. Akuma does not like her. Their motivations are unclear, even to me.

beats.headline: Classic Lucia Mar
beats.text: The net holding Carl and Princess Donut in the tower is not new. I suspect it is from before. This is classic Lucia Mar. Fopsy's reading is the sound one: a personal net from a scroll, and a secondary spell behind it, waiting for a power source. It is Power Siphon, drawing on the jewels in the active towers of Larracos, and it ends when those towers stop firing or when she turns it off. She did turn off every active spell she had, Carl. This one activated after she left.

beats.headline: A vote of No Confidence
beats.text: Carl asks where we have been. In a virtual meeting of the Syndicate Council; we are back only because the AI is throwing a fit about our missing this. A No Confidence vote on Glory is under way. The Dream and Syndicate security are shooting at everyone, and spacecraft are crash-landing on Earth. As for the rules: Tagg dies the moment Team Retribution takes his castle. A warlord off the floor forfeits and lives, but the crawl rules supersede, and his host cannot leave. Nor can he abdicate. He is the only one left. It appears impossible.

beats.headline: Acting Prime Minister
beats.text: I am waiting to be onboarded onto the Syndicate's temporary forward headquarters on the planet's surface, the ship having been shot down. With the unfortunate death of my underage nieces and nephews in orbit, I am once again eligible for office. Former Prime Minister Fopsy's relationship to the Dream being uncertain, he was passed over. I am acting Prime Minister until a real vote in a few months. It would not matter if it were permanent. I have less power than I did as a judge; the council is as gridlocked as the Lemig Sortion. Carl lays a hand on my shoulder. I am still protected.

beats.headline: I am going to level with you
beats.text: Carl. I will level with you. The AI is spread well beyond this solar system. It has killed an entire Mantis system and blown up a group of Valtay-leased manufacturing facilities, and nobody knows how it is feeding itself. Mobs from the dungeon are appearing where they should not. The Plenty control the tunnels, may be the only ones able to shut them off, and have not answered us. So ask Orren's question. He rephrases it, out loud, and the AI lets it go out live.
